question.knowledge_point: Computing the Derivative of a Quotient Given the Necessary Data
question.problem:
The values of functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=3$ are given in the table below. 

| $x$ | $f(x)$ | $g(x)$ | ${f}^{′}(x)$ | ${g}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $3$ | $2$ | $-1$ | $-4$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ |

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})$ at $x=3.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)g(x)-f(x){g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

At the point where $x=3$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=3} & =\frac{{f}^{′}(3)g(3)-f(3){g}^{′}(3)}{(g(3))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-4)\cdot (-1)-2\cdot \frac{1}{2}}{(-1)^{2}} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
